02-13.title: The Edict of Milan
02-13.description: Constantine and Licinius agree at Milan to treat Christians with benevolence across the Roman Empire, ending centuries of imperial persecution.
02-13.takeaway: A faith that had spread underground and under threat was, almost overnight, free to meet in the open. Freedom to worship is rarely permanent -- it's worth noticing when you have it.

02-23.title: The Gutenberg Bible Is Completed
02-23.description: Johannes Gutenberg's press finishes printing the first Bible produced with movable type, in Latin, in Mainz, Germany.
02-23.takeaway: For a thousand years, a Bible was a hand-copied treasure a wealthy church might own one of. Print made 'everyone could have their own copy' thinkable for the first time.

03-17.title: Patrick of Ireland's Traditional Feast Day
03-17.description: The traditionally observed date of Patrick's death -- a former slave who returned to the land of his captivity to preach the gospel across Ireland.
03-17.takeaway: Patrick's own account says he prayed constantly during years of enslavement before ever becoming the missionary history remembers. Some callings are formed in the waiting, not before it.

04-09.title: Dietrich Bonhoeffer Is Executed
04-09.description: The German pastor and theologian is hanged at Flossenburg concentration camp, days before the camp's liberation, for his resistance to the Nazi regime.
04-09.takeaway: Bonhoeffer wrote that 'when Christ calls a man, he bids him come and die.' He meant it, literally, to the end.

04-18.title: Luther Stands Before the Diet of Worms
04-18.description: Ordered to recant his writings before the Holy Roman Emperor, Martin Luther refuses unless shown by Scripture that he is wrong: 'Here I stand, I can do no other.'
04-18.takeaway: One man's conscience, tested publicly against the full weight of church and empire, reshaped how the West would read the Bible for itself.

05-20.title: The Council of Nicaea Opens
05-20.description: Bishops from across the Roman Empire gather at the emperor's invitation to settle a fierce dispute over the nature of Christ, producing the first draft of the Nicene Creed.
05-20.takeaway: Get anyone in a church today to say what they believe about who Jesus is, and the vocabulary they reach for was hammered out in arguments like this one, 1,700 years ago.

05-24.title: John Wesley's Heart Is 'Strangely Warmed'
05-24.description: At a meeting on Aldersgate Street in London, Wesley describes feeling his heart 'strangely warmed' while hearing Luther's preface to Romans read aloud.
05-24.takeaway: Wesley had already been an ordained minister and a missionary for years. Real assurance of faith found him anyway, in an ordinary room, listening to someone else's words about grace.

06-13.title: William Carey Sails for India
06-13.description: The English cobbler-turned-preacher, his wife, and their children embark for Calcutta, beginning a mission that would translate Scripture into dozens of Indian languages.
06-13.takeaway: Carey's own motto: 'Expect great things from God; attempt great things for God.' He spent the next 41 years in India without returning home once.

07-10.title: John Calvin Is Born
07-10.description: Born in Noyon, France, Calvin would later flee to Geneva and become one of the Reformation's most systematic theologians, author of the Institutes of the Christian Religion.
07-10.takeaway: Calvin never intended to end up in Geneva -- he said he was passing through and was persuaded (some accounts say threatened) to stay by the reformer Guillaume Farel. Plans rarely survive first contact with a calling.

08-28.title: Augustine of Hippo Dies
08-28.description: Augustine dies in the North African city of Hippo as Vandal armies besiege it -- the same city where, decades earlier, he'd been converted after years of resisting his mother's prayers.
08-28.takeaway: His Confessions is one of the most honest accounts of a slow, reluctant conversion ever written: 'Give me chastity and continence, but not yet.'

10-06.title: William Tyndale Is Executed
10-06.description: Tyndale, whose English New Testament gave ordinary readers direct access to Scripture for the first time, is strangled and burned at the stake near Brussels for heresy.
10-06.takeaway: His reported last words were a prayer: 'Lord, open the King of England's eyes.' Three years later, an English Bible was placed in every parish church by royal order.

10-08.title: The Council of Chalcedon Opens
10-08.description: Over 500 bishops gather to define how Christ can be both fully God and fully human in one person -- language the majority of Christian traditions still affirm today.
10-08.takeaway: Some questions about Jesus took the church centuries of careful, contested argument to answer well. Precision in theology is often the fruit of real disagreement, not its absence.

10-31.title: Luther Posts the Ninety-Five Theses
10-31.description: Martin Luther, an Augustinian monk and professor, posts his ninety-five theses against the sale of indulgences on the door of the Castle Church in Wittenberg.
10-31.takeaway: Luther meant to open an academic debate among scholars, not start a movement. He didn't get to control what happened next -- few reformers do.

default.title: The Church Has a Long Memory
default.description: No specific event is recorded for today's date yet, but the church's story spans two thousand years and every continent -- there's always more of it to learn.
